clips.brief: Manuscript. GEN 00. The round 神 seal in the new script; Oh my God cuts it open onto red; lines 0-3 as dictionary entries with red rubric headwords, on an illuminated page with a knotwork initial holding 愛 and marginalia (look illuminated) or a shakyo grid written by brush in stroke order (look shakyo); 失敬 makes the first copy.

Japanese typewriter. The selector jumps across a tray of reversed Mincho faces and strikes each sung glyph of lines 4-11 into vertical columns, every strike also printing fainter, softer and off register on two carbons beside the original; ぽいじゃん turns its glyphs to one angle; 神っぽいな cuts a seal through the stack.
Broadsheet. The press runs faster than the type until no margin is left; 夢 in wood type grows linearly past the sheet; THE END in wood type; two impressions on うええい.
Machine voice. Red takes the frame with Gott ist tot cut out of it in Fraktur. The press era ends.
Modernist. A Swiss grid dictionary, Gothic, offset dots. IQ grid gets coarser; negative print for 邪心; その〇〇 entries with cross-references to 神; My God calls.

Risograph. The hook as one four-drum poster (fluorescent pink, yellow, medium blue, black), each drum its own pass, slip, grain and dot screen, inks overprinting; one row of large kana per line, ぽいじゃん in pink knocked out of the yellow; 風 and the 神っぽいな seal cut through to red, the only colour with meaning.

The parrot. 103 BPM. A gloss page set one glyph at a time; before each syllable a fan of candidate next glyphs with true n-gram probabilities; a low-ranked sung glyph locks in red. Do you know? leaves the fan open.
Screen. JPEG re-saves step the quality down; 眠っちゃうよ one re-save per syllable; 飽きっぽい pages through; on ビーム a user posts a kaomoji cat (=^・^=)ノ and the slit fires from its hand onto red.

Repost. A light timeline where each sung line quote-reposts the last as a smaller, lower-saved screenshot of a screenshot, the chrome empties on lines 45-47, 器 shrinks to a few px through the nest, and line 50 is one post alone with nothing counted.
Machine voice. Red takes the frame again. The screen era ends.

Text-ish. Fluent and inexact; sparse pseudo-kanji in the outer margins (ish pseudo; homophone and both add same-reading kanji drift in the sung text); the sung text stays real; エピゴーネン is the highest generation; cross-references close into a loop.

Stamps, last. The hook stamps a third time, text-ish, a copy on every syllable; the view slowly zooms out as stamps land and fill the screen; each generation steps JPEG quality down; the densest frame; the last seal takes the whole frame.

The new original. Reborn Plate 0 codex folio and live 4-era specimen apparatus; lines 70-73 written stroke by stroke in the new script with red rubricated headwords (別れ, 死ぬ, 患, 踊); on the a cappella climax (いたかった人生) 人生 cuts straight through to the red substrate in both the column and the specimen box; a fresh vellum sheet sweeps over the codex and the 神 seal punches through onto Frame 0.

transitions.brief: Copy transition 0 to 1, glyphs become type: the strikes of 失 and 敬 knock the brush glyphs loose; the platen pulls the bare manuscript up into the machine, off the typewriter page that lies under it (tray, blank original, carbons); the glyphs rise, turn over into reversed Mincho slugs of type metal and drop into the empty cells of the glyph tray, a volley on each of the first three kicks of the hook (the first on the cut).

Copy transition 1 to 2, lock up the forme: through the drumless bar of 神っぽいな the typed glyphs pop off the sheets as metal sorts in random sets, each leaving its glyph cut onto red, the 神っぽいな syllables lifting their glyphs as they are sung; the press bed glides in under the carbons and the sorts glide over their slots in the chase; on the snare they drop onto the bed, the masthead first and then column by column, right to left, the typewriter tray emptying into the body; the quoins lock; an inking roller runs right to left, and behind it the impression cylinder rolls back over the forme and leaves the printed broadsheet behind it, headline first. The camera never moves.

Transition 3 to 4, the four drums print: from the last beat before the cut, a group of yellow, pink, blue and black bands, printed as riso prints them, sweeps across the frame from the left in hard 12 fps steps, the entries page in front of it and the first page of riso behind it, and the last band leaves the frame on the cut.

Transition 5 to 6, the red room is pressed: the call Do you know? cuts the sermon page open onto red, and the last fan and its candidate window open under it, after the last glyph; from the end of the call the walls of the red room close in like the plates of a hydraulic press in hard 24 fps steps, and the room lays itself out at every step: the walls push the title, the glyphs of the fan and the window, then squeeze them flat, and what cannot be squeezed any more pops out of the room and falls; 何 strikes in at the cursor on its onset and goes the same way; the last step leaves a red line, the NEW divider of line 41, on the cut, with live bored around the walls.

Transition 6 to 7, the theme switch: the color change happens inside both plates, in a snap of 6 steps of 24 fps on one S curve across the cut (mid gray on the cut itself): bored goes from its dark theme toward the light one, and tiny comes from the dark one to its own light one; each gray goes to its opposite (panels and text flip) while colours that are not gray, the red of the beam, the badges and the divider, keep their hue; the layout does not move and nothing sweeps across the frame.

Transition 8 to 9, the page is peeled off in cards, across the cut: the epigone frame is cut into 24 x 12 tiles; on each of the last three kicks before the cut a set of tiles is stamped up (the ink border and the shadow of a stamp card, a size up and a tilt for three steps) and then falls off the frame under gravity, spinning, the lower rows tending to go first; the tiles that carry the sung text of line 61 stay in place, on top of the falling cards, so every sung syllable is legible at its onset: the three stamps of ぽいなぽいなぽい go on the last beat of epigone (the last kick before the cut) and 憧れちゃうわ！ with its gloss just before the cut, so that it is already coming off when last begins, the same way; where a tile has left, the clean page of last shows, live under it before the cut and last itself after it, with its first stamps landing on a clear page; a tile that has not been stamped up yet stays the page of epigone as it stood on the cut.
